title: 1st Annual Roger Murray Lecture Series: A Conversation Between Bruce Greenwald and Tano Santos
description: A conversation with Bruce Greenwald, Robert Heilbrunn Professor Emeritus of Asset Management, and Tano Santos, David L. and M. Elsie Dodd Professor of Finance and faculty director of the Heilbrunn Center.
summary: The talk argues that sustainable value is found in companies with specialized local monopolies reinforced by network effects, such as Walmart, Google, Amazon, and Meta. In contrast, it warns against generalist strategies, poor capital allocation like Intel's, and businesses that have lost their protected status to globalization, citing General Motors and IBM as examples. The speaker also notes that while some local monopolies like John Deere are undervalued, others like Caterpillar have failed to adapt to these specific market dynamics.

claims.claim: Walmart is cited as a local competitor with distribution networks that reinforce network effects and local economies of scale.
claims.quote: if they're gonna have tough time in that area competing with local walmarts and so on but that's at least an area where the network effect is reinforced by local economies of scale
claims.speaker: Bruce Greenwald

claims.claim: Google is viewed as a sustainable monopoly in its specialized search market due to local market presence and barriers to entry.
claims.quote: they do search and they do search unbelievably well they focus on that narrow market that one function of the internet they completely dominate it they get better and better at because we all use google and they make a ton of money in that and that's not going away
claims.speaker: Bruce Greenwald

claims.claim: Microsoft is described as specialized in operating systems but lost money when trying to expand into other areas like Xbox.
claims.quote: microsoft originally only did operating systems and they kind of get a walmart strategy expanding at the edge of operating systems and when they decide that they're geniuses and try and do xbox they lose a lot of money
claims.speaker: Bruce Greenwald

claims.claim: Amazon is seen as having a sustainable business with two components: a global internet interface and a local distribution network that reinforces network effects.
claims.quote: amazon has a internet face to its customers that's going to be easy to replicate and i think what they've been smart enough to understand is that their business has two components one is the internet interface which is global essential but the second is local distribution and if they can get local distribution which is what they've got a ton of money on they will be fine
claims.speaker: Bruce Greenwald

claims.claim: Facebook (Meta) is noted to enjoy barriers to entry associated with network externalities and increasing returns in search.
claims.quote: the role of some of these big tech companies like the facebooks and the googles these companies that enjoy also some buyers to entry associated with some type of network externality in the case of facebook because they there's some natural uh increasing returns in searches
claims.speaker: Tano Santos

claims.claim: The old IBM is contrasted with modern tech companies, implying that the old generalist approach like IBM's is less relevant than specialized local markets.
claims.quote: if you compared to the old ibm that did everything right or the old uh you know rca going back further that did everything and general electric that did everything you know microsoft originally only did operating systems
claims.speaker: Bruce Greenwald

claims.claim: Apple is predicted to be in real trouble in the long run compared to other big tech monopolies.
claims.quote: on the other hand i think apple is going to be in real trouble in the long run so i think it's very important to understand area by area which of these big tech monopolies are sustainable
claims.speaker: Bruce Greenwald

claims.claim: General Motors is cited as an example of a company that lost its protected monopoly status due to globalization, leading to diminished returns on capital and less value generated by growth.
claims.quote: the companies like general motors like ibm that at the beginning of that period even ford have deeply entrenched protected essentially monopolies or oligopolies by the end of that period they are subject to competition
claims.speaker: Bruce Greenwald

claims.claim: IBM is mentioned alongside General Motors as a company that transitioned from having protected monopolies to facing competition, resulting in lower returns on capital.
claims.quote: the companies like general motors like ibm that at the beginning of that period even ford have deeply entrenched protected essentially monopolies or oligopolies by the end of that period they are subject to competition
claims.speaker: Bruce Greenwald

claims.claim: Walmart's organic growth is limited by low-income demographics where income rises slower than the overall economy, capping growth at roughly 1.5% to 2%.
claims.quote: unfortunately walmart's demographic is a low income demographic and low income demand and low income incomes are rising much less rapidly all over the world for structural reasons also related to the trend of services so that basically you know their audience or their demand is growing roughly two and a half percent less rapidly than overall two to two and a half percent subtract that from the four percent you're at one and a half maybe two at most
claims.speaker: Bruce Greenwald

claims.claim: Intel is a poor capital allocator because it spends a dollar to generate only 20 cents of value, such as with its driverless car acquisitions.
claims.quote: if these guys are pissing it away like intel trying to get into driverless cars you can look at the acquisitions and they're basically spending a dollar for 20 cents of them which means you're going to multiply that investment number by a fifth
claims.speaker: Bruce Greenwald

claims.claim: Walmart generates returns of 1.5 to 2 times the cost of capital on reinvested capital when opening new stores or converting discount stores to super centers.
claims.quote: if these guys are opening new stores in their core market like walmart was for a long time you could look at the economics of a new store or the economics of a super center conversion from a discount store and you get returns on the order of one and a half two times the cost of capital
claims.speaker: Bruce Greenwald

claims.claim: Same store sales is a direct metric for organic growth at retailers like Walmart.
claims.quote: so for instance for a retailer such as walmart with same store sales be a good metric of organic growth okay so you've got you've got direct measures like same store sales
claims.speaker: Bruce Greenwald

claims.claim: The speaker states he will not buy Amazon at the current price.
claims.quote: on the other hand i am not going to buy it at this price
claims.speaker: Bruce Greenwald

claims.claim: John Deere has local monopolies in agricultural equipment markets where it holds 90% share and is not well appreciated.
claims.quote: the one i've talked about for years because it does indicate sort of what you're looking at is the difference between deer which has moved from a manufacturing focused company to a locally based service support company where they have local software local financing local second-hand markets and local software that runs the one runs these machines and they therefore have local monopolies they have geographies where they're 90 of the agricultural equipment and nobody's getting in those uh those markets that that approach has been extraordinarily rewarding and by the way extraordinarily robust so in this crisis deer is now up over two hundred dollars this year
claims.speaker: Bruce Greenwald

claims.claim: Caterpillar is down since the beginning of the year and does not understand the local monopoly dynamics of agricultural equipment.
claims.quote: caterpillar which doesn't understand that is actually down since the beginning of the year
claims.speaker: Bruce Greenwald

claims.claim: John Deere is fully valued at this point.
claims.quote: on the other hand i will now say this at this point they are fully valued
claims.speaker: Bruce Greenwald

claims.claim: Caterpillar failed miserably when trying to enter the US farm equipment business by partnering with a German company.
claims.quote: it's uh you know a caterpillar tried they if i remember correctly they partnered up with the german farm equipment company class in marketing uh a combine that they wanted to introduce and compete for the u.s farm equipment business and they fell miserably
claims.speaker: Tano Santos
